title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are the late 'Longue Marche' notes (pp. 650 bis–787). Grothendieck is axiomatising 'discrete LT-groups'. Such a group 𝔖_0 comes with a family of exterior homomorphisms K_i : T_0 → 𝔖_0, where T_0 ≅ ℤ (or ℤ̂(1) in the profinite version). These are the 'lacets', i.e. loops or Dehn-twist-type elements. The data also includes an invariant sub-L-group Π_0 / π_0. On the surrounding pages he studies 'Lie approximations' of the system (Π_0, 𝔖_0, M). On the previous page this is the condition he calls an integral non-degenerate 'situation de Lie'. On the next page it becomes a homomorphism 𝔖_0 → 𝔊(ℚ) to a ℚ-group scheme, under which the loops become quasi-unipotent; this is close to a relative/weighted Malcev completion.

This page is a methodological Remark.

(1) In the preceding axiomatics, the group π_0 (or its profinite version π̂) itself recedes. The central objects are 𝔖_0 (or 𝔖̂_0) with its LT-structure.

(2) He suggests the right object is not π_0 but a finite-index (L-)subgroup π_0' ⊂ π_0, if one exists, satisfying two conditions:
- π_0' is itself a 'groupe à lacets';
- its loop subgroups are exactly the K_i^!(T_0).

A crossed-out first attempt defined π_0' as the subgroup generated by the K_i^!(T_0) and their conjugates (and closures).

(3) He notes that uniqueness of such a π_0' is not clear. Example: I = ∅, no punctures and hence no loops, where any finite-index subgroup seems to qualify.

(4) Historical self-diagnosis. The case he had worked with until then was 'misleading'. There one took π_0 = 𝔖_0, with 𝔖_0 identified with a low-dimensional modular/Teichmüller group: 𝔖_{0,3}^+, written alongside a (1,1)-type group. This plays on the classical coincidences between free groups of rank 2, π_{0,3} = π_1(ℙ^1 − {0,1,∞}), and congruence subgroups of the modular group SL_2(ℤ) ≅ mapping class group of type (1,1).

Had he noticed at the start that, taking π_0 = π_{0,3} as the modular starting group, the role of π_{0,3} shrinks in favour of smaller subgroups, he would have seen what in fact happened. Those smaller subgroups are of type π^𝔖 and give rise to the 𝔖^⇒ of §49 VI.

The page thus records a conceptual shift: from the full fundamental group to a canonical finite-index 'loop-generated' subgroup. It serves the general Lie/Malcev-type approximation theory of the anabelian 'Teichmüller tower' being developed on adjacent pages.
errors: No mathematical error. The existence and uniqueness of π_0' are explicitly left open, and the I = ∅ example correctly shows non-uniqueness can occur.

The identification written as '𝔖_0 = 𝔖_{0,3}^+ — (1,1)-group' is ambiguous in the manuscript. It should be read as one of the classical low-genus coincidences (π_{0,3} free of rank 2 ≅ Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL_2(ℤ) ≅ 𝔖_{1,1}/centre), not as a literal equality.

ideas.what: Replace the fundamental group π_0 by a finite-index subgroup π_0' that is itself a 'loop group' whose loop subgroups are exactly the given K_i(T_0); question of its existence and uniqueness
ideas.modern_name: Finite-index subgroups of surface/mapping class groups generated by peripheral elements or Dehn twists; 'groupes à lacets' / peripheral structure (Brenner–Lochak–Nakamura et al.)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's notion of 'groupe à lacets' (Esquisse); peripheral-structure axiomatics in later anabelian work
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme mentions groupes à lacets and the Teichmüller tower; this specific finite-index refinement does not appear there to my knowledge

ideas.what: LT-structure: a discrete group with a family of exterior homomorphisms from T_0 ≅ ℤ (loops/twists), used as input for Lie (Malcev-type) approximations with quasi-unipotent loops
ideas.modern_name: Relative / weighted completion of mapping class groups with unipotent monodromy at the boundary
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Longue Marche notes

ideas.what: Historical remark that the early identification π_0 = 𝔖_0 in the π_{0,3} / (1,1) modular case was misleading, since the role of π_{0,3} shrinks in favour of smaller subgroups (π^𝔖, 𝔖^⇒ of §49 VI)
ideas.modern_name: Low-genus coincidences F_2 ≅ π_1(ℙ^1−3 pts) ≅ Γ(2)/±1, the start of the Teichmüller tower in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; GT viewpoint: Grothendieck, Drinfeld, Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme discusses the (0,3), (0,4), (1,1) levels of the tower; this self-correction is not published

missed.claim: Open problem: does a loop-generated finite-index subgroup π_0', whose loop subgroups are exactly the K_i^!(T_0), exist canonically, and when is it unique? The axiomatic framing of this question seems not to have been pursued explicitly in the literature.
missed.quote: Il n'est pas trop clair, si un tel π_0' existe, qu'il soit nécessairement unique (pensons le cas p.ex. où I=∅ !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In anabelian geometry and GT theory, recovering peripheral (cuspidal inertia) subgroups group-theoretically is a central theme (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi–Minamide). A canonical loop-generated finite-index subgroup would bear on this. Mostly a heuristic remark, though.

missed.claim: Documents Grothendieck's own account of a methodological shift: the early focus on π_{0,3} as the base group was 'misleading', and the essential objects are smaller subgroups attached to Teichmüller-type groups.
missed.quote: Le cas qui m'avait occupé jusqu'à présent ... a été un peu "misleading"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for reconstructing how the Longue Marche approach to the Teichmüller tower evolved.

deep.surprise_reason: A short methodological and historical remark within the LT-group axiomatics. The open existence/uniqueness question for π_0' is mildly interesting but heuristic, with no finished result on the page.
transcription_corrections: 'un {+$\hat{}$-+}groupe' is more likely 'un L-groupe' (or profinite marker). The next page uses 'L-groupe', 'L-sous-groupe'.
'un groupe : "lacets"' should read 'un groupe à lacets'.

'$\hat{T}_{1,1}^+$' at the start of the line is more plausibly a script 𝔖 or T for a Teichmüller group of type (1,1), i.e. '𝔖_{1,1}^+' or 'T_{1,1}^+'. The relation to 𝔖_{0,3}^+ is written with a dash (≃ / ↔), not as part of a chain of equalities.

's'était avisé [-...-] {+au début+} de ce fait au [?] début de mon travail, où {+en prenant modulaire+}' reads more naturally as 's'était avisé de ce fait au début de mon travail, en prenant modulaire π_0 = π_{0,3} comme le groupe de départ'.
